statements.text: It also presents an important question for legislators, particularly in states that heavily subsidize the entertainment industry. They currently offer incentives for human jobs created but what do you do (tax-wise) about (potential rapid) human job displacement in favor of AI? 4/

During this strike the studios will be tempted to test AI-generated scripts. At that point, the other guilds and unions (DGA, SAG, IATSE, etc.) will have to decide whether to take a stand against working on such projects until terms around the use of AI are fully negotiated. 3/

It’s even more mystifying when you consider that good screenwriting isn’t an easy skill to replicate. Which brings us to the threat of AI. All the guilds - but especially the WGA - are in a vulnerable position in this round of negotiations. 2/

Because the studios negotiated “guardrails” around artificial intelligence with one guild (DGA) doesn’t that mean they’ll be compelled to negotiate on AI with the WGA and @sagaftra? I would think so. It’s an even bigger existential issue for those guilds, especially writers. https://t.co/bkce59cHnb
